chapter: Philadelphia, Atlantic City and the war years
title: Playing in Slappy's band at Pennsauken
summary: Slappy led a six-piece band on the river across from Camden with Ken Pope on piano and Caldwell on tenor.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, then it says -- led your own band, worked for Eugene Norman Slappy -- who's he?

Oh, he had the band in Philadelphia, but he worked over in Pennsauken, New Jersey, which is just across the river, over in -- just across, outside of Camden, New Jersey, called the Radial. And he had six pieces, but it was a very fine (unintelligible) play all them big shows.

Oh, yeah, play all them big shows. He came under Billy -- the boy from Florida. What's the name of the band now? Billy something, and he had a great band, nice band. Bass player was arranger and good musicians. I was Ken Pope on alto -- on tenor.

Very nice piano player, good musician. He had a good six piece band. That man that run that place over there was crazy about Slappy and crazy about the band because (unintelligible) came in there and said that band can't play (unintelligible).
